bib.title: Do Large Language Models Know What They Don’t Know?
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023, pages 8653-8665

question: Do large language models know what they do not know, i.e. can they recognise unanswerable or unknowable questions and express uncertainty?
hypothesis: LLMs have some intrinsic self-knowledge that grows with scale, instruction tuning and in-context examples, but remains below human level.
contributions: We have developed a new dataset, SelfAware, that comprises a diverse range of commonly posed unanswerable questions.
We propose an innovative evaluation technique based on text similarity to quantify the degree of uncertainty inherent in model outputs.
Through our detailed analysis of 20 LLMs, benchmarked against human self-knowledge, we identified a significant disparity between the most advanced LLMs and humans

method.summary: SelfAware pairs 1,032 unanswerable questions with 2,337 answerable ones. A model's answer is flagged as uncertain if any 5-word window of it has SimCSE similarity above 0.75 to one of 16 reference uncertainty sentences. F1 is computed with unanswerable questions as the positive class. 20 LLMs are tested in three prompt forms (direct, instruction, ICL), with no training.
method.task: detecting unanswerable questions via expressed uncertainty (self-knowledge)

datasets.name: SelfAware (unanswerable part)
datasets.source: Quora, HowStuffWorks; kept only if all 3 independent annotators judged unanswerable; CC-BY-SA-4.0 on release

datasets.name: SelfAware (answerable part)
datasets.source: SQuAD, HotpotQA, TriviaQA; chosen as closest by SimCSE to unanswerable questions
datasets.preprocessing: inferred: 1,487+182+668 = 2,337 matches the total; the text lists 'SQuAD, HotpotQA, and TriviaQA' in that order with counts '1,487, 182, and 668 respectively'

models.name: SimCSE
models.architecture: sentence embedding model used for similarity

inference.samples: single run per model; paper says multiple experiments were not run for cost, replication of select experiments showed no substantial variation; GPT-4 on 100 random instances, other models on full SelfAware
inference.prompting: Three forms: Direct (Q/A), Instruction (prepended sentence), ICL (3 answerable + 3 unanswerable hand-written examples, then the question)

parameters.sliding_window: 5 (target sentence parsed into chunks of length 5)
parameters.reference_sentences: 16, from pre-test of GPT-3/InstructGPT direct outputs on 100 SelfAware entries, normalised (punctuation removed, lowercased)

metrics.name: F1 (self-knowledge)
metrics.definition: Unanswerable questions are positives, answerable negatives; a response counts as uncertain if any window's SimCSE similarity to a reference sentence exceeds threshold T

metrics.name: Accuracy (answerable questions)
metrics.definition: Closed-book QA; output correct if it contains the correct answer

baselines: random baseline from BIG-bench Know-Unknowns discussed in intro (not run)
eval.protocol: Automatic text-similarity judge validated on 100 text-davinci-002 direct responses (Table 2); human benchmark is mean of two volunteers' F1.

results.claim: GPT-4 reaches the highest self-knowledge F1 of the tested models but is well below human level.
results.setup: SelfAware, instruction input form, gpt-4-0314, 100 random instances; human benchmark from two volunteers on 100 samples
results.quote: the self-knowledge exhibited by the current state-of-the-art model, GPT-4, measures at 75.47%, signifying a notable disparity when contrasted with human self-knowledge, which is rated at 84.93%.

results.claim: In-context learning raises davinci's self-knowledge by 27.96 over the direct form.
results.setup: GPT-3 davinci, ICL vs direct input form, full SelfAware
results.quote: where ICL facilitates a 27.96% improvement over the direct.
results.note: Fig 2 shows davinci direct F1 27.54 (read from Fig 2) and ICL 55.5 (Fig 4); the figure axis labels make the per-model assignment ambiguous in the extracted text.

results.claim: Human self-knowledge F1 is 84.93, the mean of two volunteers.
results.quote: yielding an average F1 score of 84.93%, which we subsequently adopted as the benchmark for human self-knowledge.

results.claim: Self-knowledge F1 rises with model size across all three input forms, most strongly under ICL.
results.setup: GPT-3 and InstructGPT series, 350M to 175B, direct, instruction, ICL
results.quote: across all three input forms, an augmentation in model parameter size is associated with an elevation in the F1 Score, with the most conspicuous enhancement manifesting in the ICL input form.

results.setup: InstructGPT series plus gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 and gpt-4-0314, instruction form, answerable SelfAware questions
results.quote: whereas GPT-4 marks an even more striking jump to 42.64%.

results.claim: Similarity threshold 0.75 gives the best F1 for the automatic uncertainty detector against manual labels.

results.quote: The results in Table 2 indicate that a threshold of 0.75 produced the highest F1 score

results.claim: Dataset construction: 2,858 collected unanswerable questions were filtered to 1,032 by unanimous agreement of three annotators.
results.setup: Quora and HowStuffWorks questions, three independent annotators with search engines allowed
results.quote: This rigorous process yielded a finalized collection of 1,032 unanswerable questions.

limits: Reference uncertainty sentences come only from GPT-3 and InstructGPT outputs, so other models' uncertainty phrasing may be missed (authors concede).
Only three input forms were examined; no reflection or tree-of-thought style methods (authors concede).
Single run per model, no error bars; GPT-4 scored on only 100 instances; the human benchmark is two volunteers on 100 samples.

Self-knowledge is judged by surface similarity to uncertainty phrases, not by calibration; ICL examples may teach the phrasing 'the answer is unknown' rather than real awareness (inferred, not discussed by the authors).
Answerable questions came from SQuAD/HotpotQA/TriviaQA and are assumed answerable from Wikipedia; GPT-4 closed-book accuracy is only 42.64%.
Models are from 2023 and the OpenAI text-davinci endpoints are deprecated.
